sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Give the difference between a mouse and a track ball.
questions.answer: A mouse is moved across a flat surface to move the pointer. A track ball is like a mouse lying on its back: it stays still and the ball is rolled with the thumb or fingers, so it needs little space and can be used on any surface — popular on portable computers.

or.q: Differentiate between a plotter and a printer.
or.answer: A printer gives hard copies of documents and pictures on normal paper sizes. A plotter is designed to draw large drawings such as building plans and blueprints using pens moved by a robotic arm; it draws curves as many short straight lines.

questions.q: What is a font face? Mention any two font families.
questions.answer: A font face is the basic typeface (design of letters) in which text is displayed. Each family shapes letters in its own way. Examples: Times New Roman and Arial (also Calibri, Verdana).

questions.q: What is the role (purpose) of the main document in mail merge?
questions.answer: The main document contains the text and graphics that remain the same in every copy, such as the body of a form letter and the return address. Merge fields are inserted in it, and they are filled with data from the data source to make personalised copies.

questions.q: What is the SUMIF() function? Give its syntax.
questions.answer: SUMIF adds only those cells that meet a given condition. Syntax: SUMIF(range, criteria, sum_range). Example: =SUMIF(B3:E3, ">99") adds only the values greater than 99; blank and text cells are ignored.

questions.q: What is Normal view in PowerPoint?
questions.answer: Normal view is the main editing view. It divides the screen into three parts: the slide pane showing the current slide, the outline/slides pane on the left, and the notes pane at the bottom for speaker notes.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: How do you set line spacing in a paragraph? What are the common line spacing values?
questions.answer: (1) Select the paragraph. (2) Home → Paragraph dialog launcher (or Line Spacing button). (3) In Indents and Spacing, choose Line spacing: Single, 1.5 lines, Double, etc., and click OK. Single spacing gives 12-point spacing, 1½ gives 18 points and double gives 24 points.

questions.q: Explain any five components of a chart.
questions.answer: (1) Chart title — the title of the whole chart. (2) Axis titles — names of the X-axis and Y-axis data. (3) X-axis categories and Y-axis values — the categories plotted and the value scale. (4) Legend — colour or pattern used for each data series. (5) Data labels — the values of the data plotted. Also tick marks (scale of axes) and gridlines (lines at major intervals).

sections.title: Long answer question. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: What is PowerPoint? Explain the different ways of creating a presentation and the views available.
questions.answer: PowerPoint is presentation software used to create slides and slide shows with text, pictures, sound and charts. Ways to create (Office Button → New): (1) Installed Templates — ready-made presentations; (2) Installed Themes / design templates — backgrounds and fonts to start with; (3) Blank Presentation — start from scratch. Views: Normal view (slide, outline and notes panes; main working view), Slide Sorter view (thumbnails for ordering and transitions) and Slide Show view (full-screen presentation with all effects; F5).

or.q: Explain any four slide layouts and how to insert, duplicate and hide slides.
or.answer: Layouts: Title Slide (title and subtitle, to begin), Title and Content (heading with a list), Two Content (two text or picture areas), Comparison (pro/con), Title Only, Blank, Section Header, Content/Picture with Caption. Insert: Home → New Slide → choose a layout. Duplicate: select the slide → Home → New Slide → Duplicate Selected Slides or Ctrl+Shift+D. Hide: right-click the slide in the slides pane → Hide Slide; it stays in the file but is not shown.
